scripts.//dev: Simulator by default. The three hardware scopes are device (both radios), ble and wifi; each has a :write twin. Without :write every write is refused — see the hardware warning in the README.
scripts.dev: npm run free-ports && concurrently -n server,client -c magenta,cyan "npm run server" "npm run web"
scripts.dev:device: npm run free-ports && concurrently -n server,client -c magenta,cyan "npm run server:device" "npm run web"
scripts.dev:device:write: npm run free-ports && concurrently -n server,client -c magenta,cyan "npm run server:device:write" "npm run web"
scripts.dev:ble: npm run free-ports && concurrently -n server,client -c magenta,cyan "npm run server:ble" "npm run web"
scripts.dev:ble:write: npm run free-ports && concurrently -n server,client -c magenta,cyan "npm run server:ble:write" "npm run web"
scripts.dev:wifi: npm run free-ports && concurrently -n server,client -c magenta,cyan "npm run server:wifi" "npm run web"
scripts.dev:wifi:write: npm run free-ports && concurrently -n server,client -c magenta,cyan "npm run server:wifi:write" "npm run web"
scripts.//start: The whole thing, fully enabled: both radios, writes ALLOWED, client bundled in production mode and neither side restarting on file changes. This is the dangerous one — read the hardware warning in the README.
scripts.start:prod: npm run free-ports && concurrently -n server,client -c magenta,cyan "npm run server:prod" "npm run web:prod"
scripts.//server: The server alone, without Metro. Same scopes as the dev scripts.
scripts.//client: The app alone, against whichever server it is pointed at.
